platform-overview.title: The platform
platform-overview.summary: ~21 containers, one schema, human approval gates on everything that ships.

sections.problem: Running real AI pipelines against personal data takes more than API keys. It needs a data layer, network isolation, and controls that survive automation running unattended.
sections.solution: Self-hosted Supabase (Postgres, Kong, GoTrue, Realtime, Storage) as the single source of truth, with a multi-tenant schema from day one. UUID keys, user_id and RLS on every table. Two production applications sit on top, a job-search command center and a document-rendering microservice.
implementation: One heavily customized docker-compose runs the fleet on a 4 vCPU / 8GB VPS.
Cloudflare Tunnel and Access sit in front of admin surfaces. Services find each other through Docker-internal DNS.
No LLM touches anything mechanical. Sorting, staleness, search, and analytics are pure computation.
sections.iteration: Every later release in this changelog ran through the same gates. Written spec, plan review, my approval, measured verification, my push.

muchane-com.title: This site, zero dependencies on purpose
muchane-com.summary: Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no build step, no remote scripts. The rejections are the design.

sections.problem: A portfolio claiming engineering judgment shouldn't ship a framework payload to render a career map.
sections.solution: Vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No build step, no remote script origins. What makes it worth reading is the rejection ledger. No frameworks. No GSAP, because WAAPI covers the zoom. No WebGL, because Canvas 2D covers the starfield. Each rejected for a stated reason rather than by taste.
implementation: Path-based routing renders hard on direct load and animates the zoom on click-through. Back pops one zoom level.
The circular carousel is dependency-free. Satellite orbits use derived geometry with clearance proofs.
85 test ids shipped ahead of the E2E suite rebuild.
sections.iteration: An 8-commit refinement pass and a 6-commit fix pass landed Aug 12 and 13. Light mode was removed, because a starfield does not survive inversion.

tailoring-quality-triad.title: Tailoring that cannot invent claims
tailoring-quality-triad.summary: Three controls shipped together. Edits the profile does not support are rejected automatically, borderline ones escalate to me, and growth is bounded so two pages stays two pages.

sections.problem: AI document tailoring fails three ways. Models invent qualifications, tailored text quietly pushes a two-page resume onto page three, and one model for every subtask either overspends or underperforms.
sections.solution: Three independent controls. A verification model at temperature 0 checks every proposed edit against my real profile, drops ungrounded claims, and escalates borderline ones to me rather than deciding alone. The asymmetry is deliberate. An unsupported edit is rejected without a human in the loop, a borderline one is not. A growth ledger caps each bullet and the whole document, which makes tailoring a reallocation rather than accretion. And a cheap model generates while a stronger model evaluates.
implementation: Document growth is bounded at 78 characters against a 6,360-character budget. No combination of legal per-bullet growth can breach the page limit.
The evaluator was chosen empirically, by comparing models on score-band placement. Six distinct output values beat compressed bands.
Every document gets human review before it goes anywhere.
sections.iteration: A standing finding from the evals reshaped what the pipeline may claim about itself. The fit score measures resume-to-job fit, not tailoring quality, and honest paraphrase should not move an honest evaluator.

shots.alt: Pipeline diagram with generate, verify, growth ledger, and human review stages, showing unsupported edits rejected automatically and borderline edits escalated to a person.
shots.caption: The tailoring pipeline. An unsupported edit is rejected automatically, a borderline one goes to a human.

paragraph-break-overlap.title: The 16% that never rendered
paragraph-break-overlap.summary: Edits spanning a paragraph break logged as applied but never rendered. A sixth of output, silently discarded.

sections.problem: The renderer resolved each tailoring edit against pristine base text, and edits spanning a paragraph break silently failed. The pipeline logged them as applied while the document shipped without them. Walking the prior corpus put the damage at roughly 16% of all edits. Paid model output, thrown away where no log could see it.
sections.solution: A crossesBreak check with strict inequality runs before slot occupancy and rejects any spanning edit so it regenerates within bounds. The alternative, teaching the renderer to apply cross-break edits, lost because constraining generation is simpler than complicating application semantics.
implementation: Boundary math validated in the ops layer before any write.
Two verification executions confirmed first-attempt renders with zero retries.
The diagnostic method mattered as much as the fix. Structural log comparison was blind to the failure, and only walking the corpus with field extraction exposed it.
sections.iteration: The investigation also exposed a contaminated control set. The "applied" labels included pre-strip operations, so the known-good corpus didn't prove what it claimed. The lesson stuck. Interrogate what a good label actually attests.

companies-surface.title: Company intelligence in one surface
companies-surface.summary: ~70 tracked companies with pure-SQL analytics. No analytics service, no ETL copy.

sections.problem: Research, postings, applications, and comp data lived across tables with no single place to answer where I stand with a company, whether my intel is stale, or where applications die in the funnel.
sections.solution: One surface. Target cards in a carousel, tabbed detail pages, and an analytics tab computed entirely in SQL against the live schema. Staleness is measured rather than guessed, because a company_views table records every look, under RLS.
implementation: The funnel with time-in-stage, response rate, posting velocity, comp bands, and fit-dimension distribution are all pure SQL.
The test suite grew past 800 vitest specs and 100 Playwright specs with zero failures.
A rail-layout defect traced back to duplicated breakpoint values, so the breakpoint was hoisted into a single exported constant.
sections.iteration: The fit-score slot shipped null-tolerant so the surface renders before the upstream score exists. Display first, data later.

shots.alt: Company intelligence grid showing six target companies with headcount, funding stage, a recent research finding, a freshness indicator, and an interest score.
shots.caption: Company intelligence surface, illustrative data.

ats-ingestion-feed-complete.title: Ingestion that closes its own ghosts
ats-ingestion-feed-complete.summary: One invariant governs closure. No feed may kill a posting unless it can prove it saw everything.

sections.problem: Multi-ATS ingestion raises two hard problems. Dedup without fake placeholder keys, since Postgres treats NULL as unequal to NULL. And closure, because marking a posting dead requires knowing the feed you just read was complete. A partial feed treated as complete mass-closes live postings.
sections.solution: Adapters per source feed a shared core, governed by one invariant. Any trigger path that is not a complete company feed must declare its feed incomplete, or the core will close everything it didn't see. Per-posting liveness checks lost on cost, since that approach spends a request per posting against rate-limited vendors.
implementation: Greenhouse runs every four hours and pulls roughly 1,900 postings per cycle with full content. Ashby follows ten minutes later, the retention sweep after that. The stagger keeps a 4-vCPU box out of contention.
Sequential batch processing ahead of dedup checks prevents race-condition duplicates.
A designed Lever adapter extends the invariant with a sentinel-probe completeness gate. The feed must prove it is complete before it may close anything.
sections.iteration: The invariant hardened into system law. A planned single-URL ingest path is designed around it and forced to declare its feeds incomplete. No mass-close incidents on record since.

shots.alt: Job triage table with filter tabs, sortable columns, and twelve ingested postings showing company, status, posting age, title, team, office type, and location.
shots.caption: Triage table over ingested postings, illustrative data.

updated-at-phantom-writer.title: Hunting a phantom writer
updated-at-phantom-writer.summary: updated_at churned on every cycle. The writer wasn't on the table being written.

sections.problem: The updated_at column on jobs rows churned every ingestion cycle even when nothing changed, which poisoned staleness logic and masked real updates. The jobs table's own triggers and write paths were clean.
sections.solution: Widen the search. Inventory triggers on every table that writes into the target, not just the target itself. The writer turned out to be a trigger on the job_locations junction table, touching the parent row on every location re-upsert. It was dropped, and every write path now diffs before writing.
implementation: A second latent bug fell in the same pass. The update mapping had been NULL-writing two score columns on every cycle.
Diff-before-write became the standard for every update path.
sections.iteration: The junction-table lesson is now a standing diagnostic rule, and the repaired timestamp feeds the staleness chips with a signal worth trusting.

kanban-status-history.title: Kanban with measured time-in-stage
kanban-status-history.summary: A DB trigger writes every status transition to an append-only history table, so funnel analytics compute from real events rather than a mutable column.

dual-path-network.title: Two paths to one database
dual-path-network.summary: App traffic rides Kong under JWT-enforced RLS. Automation rides an isolated internal network. The tiers can't reach each other.

sections.problem: The automation engine needs upsert semantics the REST layer cannot express, multi-column conflict resolution on nullable keys, where Postgres treats NULL as unequal to NULL and matching fails outright. The naive fixes are all bad. Placeholder sentinels pollute the schema, and exposing Postgres to the app tier widens the attack surface.
sections.solution: Two physically separate data paths. Application traffic goes Nginx Proxy Manager to Kong to services under JWT-enforced Row Level Security, so apps see only their user's rows. System traffic runs n8n straight to Postgres over an internal Docker bridge the web-facing proxy has no route to. Routing automation through PostgREST lost because the API cannot express the writes. Sentinel values lost because they make the schema dishonest.
implementation: Port 5432 is never exposed publicly, and system traffic never leaves the internal bridge.
Services are addressed by Docker-internal DNS, never by IP.
The convention is codified. Postgres nodes for writes, Supabase nodes for simple reads, sequential batches ahead of dedup checks.
A compromised frontend cannot reach the database port. It sits on a different tier.
sections.iteration: Every later pipeline shipped without needing a new network path. The NULL lesson became a standing rule to check existence before upserting on nullable fields.

shots.alt: Architecture diagram showing an application tier and a system tier that share one Postgres database with no route between them.
shots.caption: Two paths to one database. Application traffic under RLS, automation on an isolated internal network.

char-budget-gate.title: Stop asking LibreOffice how many pages a Word document has
char-budget-gate.summary: Identity round-trip testing proved the renderer miscounts the unmodified template. The page gate became a character budget.

sections.problem: The document renderer gated output on LibreOffice's page count, and identity round-trip testing proved LibreOffice counts the two-page Calibri template as three pages even with genuine Microsoft Calibri installed. Valid documents were being rejected. A second bug compounded it, since the spec endpoint reported a budget equal to the base length and told the tailoring model it had zero room to expand.
sections.solution: Stop asking a renderer that disagrees with Word about the untouched template. A per-template sidecar declares canonical pages and a hard character budget, 6,360 characters for the primary template. Chasing font-metric parity inside LibreOffice lost because the identity test showed no amount of tuning would converge.
implementation: Balanced bold markers are stripped before counting so formatting doesn't consume budget.
The error-response shape was preserved for the pipeline consumer, with new diagnostic fields for actual characters, budget, and per-field breakdown.
All 44 pytest tests pass in-container.
sections.iteration: The diagnostic fields later made retry accounting debuggable, and in August the budget idea moved upstream as the growth ledger. Constrain generation, not just output.

n8n-bloat-surgery.title: 3.65GB of dead execution logs
n8n-bloat-surgery.summary: 3.65GB of success-run logs cut to 73MB by retention policy, with a manual test fired to prove failure debugging still captures everything.

agent-hardening.title: A locked-down user for the coding agent
agent-hardening.summary: The VPS coding agent runs as a dedicated no-sudo user with command blocks, a logged network wrapper, and session and incident logs. Autonomy inside enforced guardrails rather than trust.

swap-provisioning.title: Swap before the OOM killer wins
swap-provisioning.summary: The VPS was running with zero swap and the OOM killer was firing immediately under pressure. 4GB provisioned, about 2GB in steady use.

backup-integrity.title: Backups that restore, not backups that exist
backup-integrity.summary: A PTY flag was corrupting dumps in transit. It was dropped, historical dumps were tested one by one, and a verified-restore roadmap is in place.

workflow-status-lights.title: Green and amber lights
workflow-status-lights.summary: Every pipeline upserts a heartbeat row to workflow_runs, surfaced as status lights in the app footer. Health at a glance instead of at failure.
